mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has stabilized at -18.9% over the last four weeks with minimal week-on-week volatility (range: -23.3% to -18.9%). This plateau signals equilibrium in suppressed retail demand. Absent a shock to WORKPLACES or TRANSIT, retail mobility will remain flat or decline further over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined from -23.3% (t-3w) to -18.9% (t-0w) then stabilized
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -15% in any week over the next 28 days without a corresponding rise in WORKPLACES or TRANSIT of more than 5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility (16.6% at t-0w) combined with suppressed RETAIL_REC (-18.9%) indicates consumers are sheltering in place. If RESIDENTIAL remains above 16% over the next two weeks, home-based consumption substitutes for retail visits, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed below -15%.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 16% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -12% while RESIDENTIAL stays above 16% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has declined from -21.3% (t-3w) to -21.6% (t-0w), indicating sustained workplace suppression. TRANSIT has remained stable at approximately -32% across all four weeks. This persistent dual suppression of work and transit activity will constrain retail recovery, as commuting-linked retail visits remain blocked.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES range -21.3% to -23.7% across four weeks
fact:TRANSIT range -30.7% to -32.7% across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -10% while both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below -20% for the entire next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stabilized near -3% (range: -3.3% to -0.3%), indicating essential retail access is maintained. If GROCERY_PHARM remains above -5% over the next week, it signals policy permits essential retail operations. This permission regime will extend to non-essential RETAIL_REC, lifting it by at least 3 percentage points within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -2% for one week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise above -16% within two weeks of GROCERY_PHARM rising above -2%.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS range -16.1% to -20.9% across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise above -15% within four weeks of PARKS rising above -10%.

Combined with WORKPLACES rising above -15% in the same week, this dual signal will lift RETAIL_REC by 5+ percentage points within two weeks as commute-linked retail activity resumes.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise above -14% within two weeks of both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rising simultaneously to the specified thresholds.

If this linear improvement continues at 1+ percentage point per week, RETAIL_REC will reach -14% or higher within four weeks, representing a net positive shift from the baseline suppression.
